objects.name: InferenceSession
objects.role: Selects devices, runtime thread settings, extensions and artifact-store policy. Adds the host CPU if absent. A session is neither a model nor a separate OS process.

objects.name: CPU / Accelerator handles
objects.role: Device handles identify configured targets. Compilation may use virtual devices; execution requires real device support. CPU is included in the session even when an accelerator is selected.

objects.name: GraphSpec + Llama module
objects.role: The built-in Llama Graph API route supplies a module and symbolic input types. GraphSpec.trace delegates to Llama3.trace. ModuleV3 takes a different staging route.

objects.name: Symbolic input contract
objects.role: Input types describe dtype, shape (including symbolic dimensions), and placement. They are descriptions rather than per-inference tensor values.

objects.name: Graph / MLIR module
objects.role: Graph owns symbolic graph structure. Forward runs during construction to record operations; it does not compute model outputs on a GPU.

objects.name: KernelLibrary declarations
objects.role: The graph imports kernel declarations. compile_async seeds those declarations into the module so native graph compilation can skip repeating package loading.

objects.name: Symbolic graph operations
objects.role: Embedding, decoder blocks and projections become graph IR on the Llama trace route. The Add example in chapter 03 demonstrates a registration mechanism, not the full Llama kernel schedule.

objects.name: Graph.output contract
objects.role: Flattens outputs, adds dependency chains, sets signatures and mo.output, names the interface, then verifies MLIR. This finalizes the symbolic contract before native compilation.

objects.name: _COMPILATION_LOCK
objects.role: Serializes Graph/Module native compilation in this process. Acquire before native scheduling; release on setup failure or via the compile completion callback. It is not an IPC semaphore.

objects.name: Pending compilation result
objects.role: compile_async returns a CompiledModel backed by a pending native result. compile waits; export or initialization can also resolve pending compilation. A handle does not itself execute the model.

objects.name: Runtime CPU worker pool
objects.role: Native compileModel schedules a CPU runtime task. Native initialization uses a CPU worker continuation. No separate compiler process or fixed thread count is implied.

objects.name: Compiler-owned MLIR clone
objects.role: The frontend clones the input module before lowering, resolves compiler settings and checks whether declarations are already seeded. The caller graph and this transformed clone are distinct.

objects.name: Native model-IR → MEF cache
objects.role: If enabled and available, the frontend derives a cache key from the module/options/version and returns a matching MEF before lowering. This cache is separate from Python MefStore.

objects.name: MO stage
objects.role: Imports definitions when needed; performs configured shape/symbolic optimization, layout inference and target validation. Pass scheduling does not establish which exact Llama transformations occur.

objects.name: MAP stage
objects.role: Fuses eligible structured computations, allocates accumulating buffers and outlines kernel bodies. Several graph operations may share a kernel; this animation makes no kernel-count claim.

objects.name: MOGG stage
objects.role: Legalizes calls and operands, outlines routines, then transitions into the runtime-model representation. These are compiler representations, not OS components.

objects.name: MGP stage
objects.role: Plans buffer reuse and allocations, lowers primitives and dependencies, handles configured device-graph work, merges equivalent routines and emits Mojo. Device-graph passes are distinct from Graph.output.

objects.name: Mojo Add registration
objects.role: The real Add struct is registered as mo.add. Its elementwise overloads use dtype/SIMD-width or tile-layout parameters. Registration provides an implementation building block; it does not imply one launch per graph op.

objects.name: Emitted Mojo routines
objects.role: MGP emits Mojo routines before the enclosing graph pipeline schedules kernel JIT and final runtime-call lowering. The handwritten Add registration and emitted model routines have different roles.

objects.name: Mojo parse / semantic checks
objects.role: The compiler walkthrough describes parsing/name/type resolution, semantic control-flow and lifetime checks, then LIT lowering. This is a compiler architecture view, not a captured compile trace.

objects.name: KGEN pre-elaboration
objects.role: Pre-elaboration optimization reduces parametric IR before specialization. Compile-time generators retain parameters until elaboration.

objects.name: Elaboration / concrete functions
objects.role: Elaboration resolves generators and compile-time parameters into concrete functions/types. dtype, SIMD width and tile layout are illustrated by Add; this page does not choose actual target specializations.

objects.name: LLVM / target lowering
objects.role: Concrete functions undergo lowering/optimization and target code generation. CPU and GPU targets have distinct backend requirements. A target binary is code; no inference input has run yet.

objects.name: Compiled kernel code
objects.role: JIT-compiled routines and final runtime calls contribute to the lowered executable artifact. Fusion and routine reuse mean graph-op counts, routine counts and runtime launch counts differ.

objects.name: MEF bytes / file
objects.role: convertMGPToMEF prepares device primitives and serializes the lowered model. MEF can include constant resources. External weights, initialization state and per-call inputs remain separate concepts.

objects.name: Python MefStore
objects.role: Explicit session store overrides the process-wide default. Graph name/signature select the artifact; optional verify_body checks its fingerprint. The store lock protects its metadata. Declined keys compile normally; missing accepted artifacts raise.

objects.name: Export manifest
objects.role: Export records key, graph name/signature/body fingerprint, writes MEF and persists the manifest. Exporting and importing cannot both be requested on the same session.

objects.name: CompiledModel / CompiledModels
objects.role: Wraps compiled/deserialized native models. It cannot execute. It can be initialized repeatedly. read(MEF) bypasses rebuilding the Python Graph; a GraphSpec reuse route has already traced.

objects.name: Named weight registry
objects.role: init_all checks expected weight names and CPU/device category when Graph metadata is available, then contiguity. read/path-compiled artifacts have no Python expected-weight metadata. Weights are distinct from input buffers.

objects.name: Native model setup
objects.role: Model.setup receives CPU runtime, weights registry and device-context map. createExecutableModel waits for setup before returning a usable executable. Compilation alone does not initialize this device state.

objects.name: Persistent executable context
objects.role: ExecutableModel retains chain, MGP context, weights registry and extra initialization/device arguments. Execution passes these fixed values alongside per-call inputs.

objects.name: Initialized Model / ExecutableModel
objects.role: Normal init_all returns Models keyed by sym_name. These hold runnable native models. Virtual mode yields CompileOnlyModel stand-ins when graph names are known; they explicitly refuse execution.

objects.name: Per-call input buffers
objects.role: Model.execute accepts Buffer, supported DLPack arrays or scalar inputs. Checks contiguity, wraps DLPack or constructs scalar Buffers, then prepares native inputs. These values differ from symbolic input types.

objects.name: Native input validation
objects.role: Native input handling checks input count, shape/dtype contract and device placement, extracts buffer storage and marshals AsyncValues. Invalid inputs can fail before graph execution.

objects.name: AsyncValue register file
objects.role: MEF registers hold values that can be pending, ready or errors. Ready values activate users immediately; pending results install readiness callbacks. This is dependency synchronization rather than a MAX Serve request queue.

objects.name: MEF invocation / executor
objects.role: Invocation decodes register/primitive tables and allocates executor state. Runnable work follows operand readiness. Execution can dispatch asynchronous work; the executor is not a model-worker process.

objects.name: Ready primitive worklist
objects.role: The worklist decrements atomic not-ready counts. A primitive runs when its readiness gate clears. Nonstrict primitives can receive indirect values; readiness and errors govern downstream work.

objects.name: Device runtime / driver
objects.role: Execution uses configured device contexts and device-appropriate primitives. Exact launch streams, driver calls and physical allocation depend on the target; this animation does not measure them.

objects.name: CPU / GPU computation
objects.role: Target code executes on real configured hardware. GPU kernel overlap, duration, occupancy and memory traffic require runtime evidence. Animated movement is a teaching aid.

objects.name: Returned output buffers
objects.role: extractDriverResults awaits runtime result values, reports errors, drops the internal chain and wraps tensor results into device buffers; Python returns Buffer objects. A return does not mean a universal device-wide barrier or host copy.

phases.title: Session & graph
phases.detail: Create the session and trace the built-in Llama Graph API route. Input types are symbolic; forward records operations. Graph.output defines/verifies outputs. Session, graph, weight values and runtime inputs are different objects. Direct read(MEF) can bypass graph rebuilding.
phases.ascii:
GraphSpec(module, input_types) → Llama3.trace → Graph(forward)
  input metadata → symbolic operations → Graph.output → verified IR
InferenceSession(devices) → native runtime / compilation context
Alternative: read(existing.mef) → CompiledModel, without a new Graph

phases.title: Graph compiler
phases.lesson: Transform graph IR into a runtime program.
phases.detail: Native Graph compilation is scheduled on a CPU runtime worker under a process-wide lock. Lower a clone through MO, MAP, MOGG and MGP. Configured native cache hits bypass lowering. These frames group compiler roles inside the application, not separate OS processes.
phases.ascii:
compile(Graph) → compile_async → acquire _COMPILATION_LOCK
  capsule → CompilationRequest → CPU runtime task → clone MLIR
  native cache HIT → MEF; MISS → MO → MAP → MOGG → MGP
  MGP → emitted Mojo → JIT → runtime calls → MEF
  completion callback releases lock; compile() waits

phases.title: Mojo kernels
phases.lesson: Connect a graph op to compiled target code.
phases.detail: The real mo.add registration shows parameterized Mojo implementation. MAX emits/compiles routines; the Mojo compiler performs semantic/lifetime checks, parametric optimization, elaboration and target lowering. This chapter combines a source example with documented compiler architecture, rather than claiming a recorded Add or Llama compilation.
phases.ascii:
@extensibility.register("mo.add") → Mojo Add implementation
MGP → Mojo routines → kernel JIT / runtime-call lowering
Mojo: parse / types → semantic / lifetime checks → LIT lowering
  → KGEN optimization → elaboration → concrete functions
  → post-elaboration optimization → LLVM / target code
An op can be fused; this is not one GPU launch per op.

phases.title: MEF preparation
phases.lesson: Store executable code, then choose a reuse route.
phases.detail: Cold compilation serializes MEF. Native model-IR caching and Python MefStore are distinct. Export can occur before runtime initialization. GraphSpec-based import still traces; direct read does not need a new Graph. A declined import key compiles normally, while a missing accepted artifact is an error. Pre-JIT stopping creates no MEF.
phases.ascii:
Cold: lowered MGP → prepare primitives → serialize MEF → CompiledModel
Native cache: matching module/options → cached MEF
Store export: compile → claim_export → export_mef → manifest
Store import: trace → claim_import → compile(path) → deserialize
Direct: read(MEF) → deserialize (no new Graph)
Declined key → compile; missing accepted key → MissingArtifactError

phases.title: Initialize weights
phases.detail: Bind actual named weight buffers after compilation. Graph metadata supports name/device-category validation; contiguity is checked on real initialization. Native setup binds contexts and waits for setup dependencies. Virtual mode creates explicit compile-only stand-ins if names are known, and rejects path artifacts with unknown names.
phases.ascii:
CompiledModel + weights_registry(name → buffer)
  → expected-name/device checks when captured → contiguity checks
  → _load_all → Model.setup(CPU, registry, device map)
  → await setup chain/context → Model keyed by sym_name
Virtual: known names → CompileOnlyModel; execute refuses
Virtual: path/read artifact with unknown names → ValueError

phases.title: Run inference
phases.detail: Per-call Buffers are validated and marshaled as AsyncValues. Native execution releases the GIL, passes persistent context/weights with inputs, and invokes MEF. Primitive readiness activates users or installs callbacks for pending values. Result extraction awaits runtime results and returns Buffers. Target-level synchronization and transfers are backend-specific.
phases.ascii:
Model.execute(inputs) → Buffer / DLPack / scalar conversion
  → validate dtype/shape/device → prepare AsyncValues
  → release GIL → ExecutableModel.execute
  fixed chain/context/weights + inputs → MEF invocation
  readiness counts / worklist → primitive dispatch
  pending result → andThenSync → downstream users
  await runtime results → drop chain → return output Buffers

events.title: Create InferenceSession
events.detail: The session selects runtime devices and compilation policy. Host CPU is added if absent.

events.title: Use a GraphSpec recipe
events.detail: Module and symbolic input types describe the Llama computation, before per-call buffers exist.

events.title: Graph records forward symbolically
events.detail: The Graph constructor creates MLIR and runs the forward callback to record operations.

events.title: Graph.output verifies the contract
events.detail: Set output signatures, chains, mo.output and names; verify MLIR. No numerical inference ran.

events.title: Direct MEF read needs no new Graph
events.detail: This route starts from an existing artifact. It bypasses rebuilding/tracing the Python Graph.

events.title: Choose an existing artifact route
events.detail: Explicit import chooses an artifact after trace; read starts from bytes. Graph compiler lowering is skipped.

events.title: Import store declines this key
events.detail: claim_import returns None. The Graph follows normal compilation rather than the import path.

events.title: Enter compile_async from compile
events.detail: Prepare Graph weight-device expectations, extension libraries and seeded kernel declarations. Native scheduling comes next.

events.title: Acquire the process-wide compilation lock
events.detail: Graph/Module compilation stays protected until the native completion callback releases this lock.

events.title: Schedule native compile on the CPU pool
events.detail: The capsule becomes a CompilationRequest. compileModel adds a CPU runtime task and returns its async result.

events.title: Return an async-backed CompiledModel handle
events.detail: compile_async wraps the native result. It remains pending in this illustration while native work continues; compile waits for completion.

events.title: Clone the input module / resolve options
events.detail: Lowering owns a clone. Seeded kernel declarations prevent repeated package imports.

events.title: Native cache hit returns MEF early
events.detail: Assume native model-IR caching is enabled and a matching artifact exists. Compiler passes are bypassed.

events.title: MO: shapes, layouts and target legality
events.detail: Configured high-level passes prepare graph IR. This is a pass schedule, not measured Llama fusion.

events.title: MAP: eligible fusion and outlined bodies
events.detail: Structured computations can fuse. Accumulating buffers and outlined bodies prepare kernel work.

events.title: MOGG: legalize calls and outline routines
events.detail: Prepare kernel calls and operands, then lower into the runtime-model representation.

events.title: MGP: plan buffers, dependencies and primitives
events.detail: Reuse/allocation planning, configured device-graph work and primitive lowering precede Mojo emission.

events.title: Kernel compilation is bypassed on this route
events.detail: Cached/imported/read artifacts already contain compiled content. No new model kernel JIT is shown.

events.title: Find the real mo.add → Mojo Add registration
events.detail: Add provides parameterized SIMD and tile overloads. This source example illustrates registration rather than a specific Llama launch.

events.title: MGP emits Mojo routines
events.detail: The enclosing MAX pipeline schedules JIT after Mojo emission, then final runtime-call lowering.

events.title: Mojo compiler: parse / types / lifetime checks
events.detail: The documented compiler architecture checks source/semantics and lowers LIT. Detailed JIT plumbing can vary by entry point.

events.title: Optimize parametric KGEN
events.detail: Reduce and simplify parametric IR before specialization.

events.title: Elaborate compile-time parameters
events.detail: Resolve generators into concrete functions/types. Add illustrates dtype, width and layout parameters.

events.title: Lower / optimize into target code
events.detail: Concrete functions pass through post-elaboration and target lowering. CPU/GPU backends differ.

events.title: Pre-JIT inspection stops before artifact creation
events.detail: Deliberate stop after Mojo emission. convertMOToMEF returns an error; no MEF is serialized/cached and no model can execute.

events.title: Serialize lowered MGP into MEF
events.detail: Prepare device-specific primitives, translate to MEF and copy serialized resources into the artifact buffer.

events.title: Resolve cached MEF bytes
events.detail: Native cache supplied the buffer before graph/Mojo lowering. It still represents an uninitialized artifact.

events.title: Import a matched Graph artifact
events.detail: Graph trace already occurred. claim_import returns a path; compile(path) deserializes the MEF rather than lowering new graph IR.

events.title: Missing accepted artifact raises
events.detail: An accepted key with no recorded artifact raises MissingArtifactError. It does not silently fall back to compilation.

events.title: Read MEF directly into CompiledModel
events.detail: read(path or file-like bytes) creates an uninitialized artifact. No new symbolic Graph or native graph lowering is required.

events.title: Compilation result resolves / compile waits
events.detail: Graph compilation completion releases the lock. compile waits on the native result. The compiled artifact still cannot execute.

events.title: Existing artifact is ready for initialization
events.detail: A deserialized artifact holds compiled models without runtime weight binding.

events.title: Claim export identity and write MEF
events.detail: Export before initialization. The store records signature/body fingerprint; export_mef writes the artifact and write_manifest persists metadata.

events.title: Pass actual named weight buffers to init_all
events.detail: Graph-based compilation retains expected weight metadata. Direct read / path compilation lack that Python metadata; native artifact contracts still apply.

events.title: Reject a noncontiguous registered weight
events.detail: Normal-device initialization checks each registered weight and raises ValueError for this deliberately invalid layout.

events.title: Virtual mode returns compile-only stand-ins
events.detail: Graph names are known for Graph/Module compilation. init_all returns CompileOnlyModel values rather than executable models.

events.title: Virtual initialization rejects unknown graph names
events.detail: Path/read artifacts carry no Python graph-name list here. Virtual mode raises instead of pretending initialization succeeded.

events.title: Validate / bind weights on real devices
events.detail: Check captured names and CPU/device category when available; always check registered buffer contiguity on this normal path.

events.title: Native setup binds runtime/device context
events.detail: A CPU worker continuation calls model.setup with registry and device map, then awaits setup dependencies.

events.title: Return initialized Model keyed by sym_name
events.detail: Setup finished. The Model retains its executable context and can now accept per-call inputs.

events.title: CompileOnlyModel refuses execute
events.detail: Virtual compilation can inspect/export code, but the stand-in cannot execute or allocate device-dependent state.

events.title: Convert per-call inputs to Buffers
events.detail: Accept Buffer, supported DLPack arrays or scalars after contiguity checks. Inputs are values, unlike symbolic input types.

events.title: Validate shape / dtype / device, marshal AsyncValues
events.detail: Native handling validates input spec and placement, extracts storage and prepares runtime values.

events.title: Release GIL / invoke the executable
events.detail: Native execution releases the Python GIL. Fixed chain/context/weights and extra setup arguments accompany each call’s inputs.

events.title: Decode registers / primitive tables
events.detail: MEF invocation allocates per-call executor state and starts primitives whose dependency gates permit execution.

events.title: Ready operands activate primitive work
events.detail: Atomic not-ready counts drop. A ready primitive gets its implementation and arguments; nonstrict primitives can take indirect values.

events.title: Device-appropriate work computes results
events.detail: Primitives use target code and configured device context. Arrow movement illustrates dispatch, not a measured GPU stream or timeline.

events.title: Pending result installs a readiness callback
events.detail: For a pending AsyncValue, andThenSync retains the executor and processes users when the value becomes ready.

events.title: Await runtime results / return output Buffers
events.detail: Driver result extraction awaits values, propagates errors, drops the internal chain, preserves device placement and wraps returned tensors.

compile_async.purpose: Prepare a Graph, Module, or artifact path for asynchronous native compilation.

notes.title: Source-kind dispatch
notes.text: Paths and in-memory Graphs follow different branches. A Graph contributes its MLIR module and extension libraries.

notes.title: Retain initialization expectations
notes.text: The graph's weight declarations supply expected device metadata, checked when weight buffers are bound.

notes.title: Seed declarations
notes.text: Reuse kernel declarations already loaded by the Graph's KernelLibrary before the native module handoff.

notes.title: Return an artifact handle
notes.text: The handle carries the asynchronous result and graph names. compile() below waits for completion.

compile_async.label: Prepare a Graph, Module, or artifact path for asynchronous native compilation.

compile_graphs.purpose: Trace graph recipes, compile artifacts, then initialize their weights.

notes.title: Trace each compilation group
notes.text: The ordinary Llama decoder has one spec. Multiple grouped roles can instead share a graph Module.

notes.title: Compilation boundary
notes.text: The completed graph or module is compiled or resolved through configured artifact reuse.

notes.title: Bind after compilation
notes.text: Collect weights by name, reject conflicting values, and initialize all models in the compiled artifact.

compile_graphs.label: Trace graph recipes, compile artifacts, then initialize their weights.

compile_module.purpose: Cross the Python/C++ boundary with the MLIR module capsule.

notes.title: Serialize native compilation
notes.text: The process-wide lock is acquired before scheduling. Synchronous setup errors release it immediately.

notes.title: Payload
notes.text: The capsule identifies the MLIR module; extensions, a pipeline name, and the fusion option accompany it.

notes.title: Asynchronous lifetime
notes.text: Completion releases the lock through a callback. Returning a pending handle does not end the protected compile interval.

compile_module.label: Cross the Python/C++ boundary with the MLIR module capsule.

compile_reuse.purpose: Select normal compilation, configured MEF import, or MEF export.

notes.title: Choose the store
notes.text: Use the explicit session store if present, otherwise the default. Non-Graph modules take the regular compile route.

notes.title: Import or decline
notes.text: A matching artifact path is passed to compile. A store that declines this graph falls back to compiling the graph.

notes.title: Export mode
notes.text: Write the compiled artifact under the store's claimed export location.

compile_reuse.label: Select normal compilation, configured MEF import, or MEF export.

compile_wait.purpose: Wait for asynchronous compilation and surface errors to the caller.

notes.title: Synchronous completion
notes.text: Schedule compilation, wait on its result, and distinguish requested pre-JIT stopping from a compile failure.

compile_wait.label: Wait for asynchronous compilation and surface errors to the caller.

compiled_create.purpose: Compile in-memory source or read a model artifact from a path.

notes.title: Graph-source branch
notes.text: A source pointer selects the MOF frontend, which produces a MEF buffer. read then builds compiled-model objects from that buffer.

notes.title: Already compiled path
notes.text: A MEF path is read directly. Entering an API named compile does not imply compiler passes run.

compiled_create.label: Compile in-memory source or read a model artifact from a path.

convert_mef.purpose: Run graph compilation, then serialize the lowered model to MEF.

notes.title: Execute compiler passes
notes.text: A failed pipeline returns graph diagnostics rather than an artifact.

notes.title: Intentional early stop
notes.text: Pre-JIT inspection ends after Mojo emission; the partially lowered result is not serialized to the MEF cache.

notes.title: Artifact boundary
notes.text: Serialize the successfully lowered module and return its MEF buffer.

convert_mef.label: Run graph compilation, then serialize the lowered model to MEF.

engine_compile.purpose: Schedule compilation on a CPU worker and resolve an asynchronous result.

notes.title: Worker boundary
notes.text: The captured request is processed by compileModelSync on the CPU worker; error and telemetry handling resolve the returned handle.

engine_compile.label: Schedule compilation on a CPU worker and resolve an asynchronous result.

engine_sync.purpose: Supply device configuration and create native compiled-model objects.

notes.title: Target context
notes.text: Pass configured devices into the compilation request, then dispatch to CompiledModels::create.

engine_sync.label: Supply device configuration and create native compiled-model objects.

frontend.purpose: Clone the graph module, configure lowering, and consult the native MEF cache.

notes.title: Compiler-owned module
notes.text: Lowering transforms a clone of the incoming module. Weight resources are owned by its MLIR context.

notes.title: Resolve compiler options
notes.text: Collect configuration and detect pre-seeded kernel declarations before deriving cache behavior.

notes.title: Cache-hit return
notes.text: When model-IR caching is enabled and a matching artifact exists, return it before convertMOToMEF runs.

notes.title: Cache miss
notes.text: Compile/serialize, then attempt to insert the resulting buffer in the cache.

frontend.label: Clone the graph module, configure lowering, and consult the native MEF cache.

gc_pipeline.purpose: Build the ordered sequence of representation conversions and compiler stages.

notes.title: High-level graph stage
notes.text: The mo-pre-map dump follows MO processing; subsequent stage names distinguish conversions from stage-local transforms.

notes.title: Representation transition
notes.text: Stable-tensor marking precedes MO-to-MAP conversion.

notes.title: Kernel representation
notes.text: MOGG preparation precedes conversion into the MGP runtime model.

notes.title: JIT configuration
notes.text: JIT target and compilation options are only configured when JIT is enabled.

notes.title: Compile kernels
notes.text: After MGP/Mojo emission, run JIT compilation, strip kernel declarations, and finish runtime-call lowering.

gc_pipeline.label: Build the ordered sequence of representation conversions and compiler stages.

graph_init.purpose: Create MLIR graph structure and optionally trace a Python callable.

notes.title: Symbolic dimensions
notes.text: Names from symbolic tensor/buffer dimensions become graph parameters.

notes.title: MLIR ownership
notes.text: Use a supplied module or create one, then create mo.graph with input types and initially empty result types.

notes.title: Kernel declarations and graph mode
notes.text: Import the kernel library and mark the graph if explicit device-graph construction was requested.

notes.title: Automatic finalization
notes.text: Run the callable inside the active graph context. Its return form determines how output is invoked.

graph_init.label: Create MLIR graph structure and optionally trace a Python callable.

graph_output.purpose: Finish the graph's output contract and verify the completed graph.

notes.title: 1 · Flatten outputs
notes.text: Retain the Python output structure; flatten its leaves. A string leaf is rejected because unpacking a dict into its keys is usually a mistake.

notes.title: 2 · Normalize values and chains
notes.text: Convert leaves to Graph Values and include final chain values when the graph has chain inputs. Chains preserve dependency ordering.

notes.title: 3 · Set both signatures
notes.text: The actual argument and result types define functionType and the kgen generator signature. Symbolic dimensions can remain symbolic.

notes.title: 4 · Append the terminator
notes.text: mo.output identifies which SSA values leave the graph. This records IR; it does not launch inference.

notes.title: 5 · Name the interface
notes.text: Ordinal input/result names are written for the engine. The Python output tree is retained separately.

notes.title: 6 · Verify the graph
notes.text: Clear temporary bookkeeping and invoke MLIR graph verification. Failure reports diagnostics. Numerical correctness and target compilation remain separate checks.

graph_output.label: Finish the graph's output contract and verify the completed graph.

init_all.purpose: Validate weight buffers and initialize models in a compiled artifact.

notes.title: Weight contract
notes.text: Check names and expected CPU/device category captured from the graph. These checks occur after graph finalization and compilation.

notes.title: Buffer layout check
notes.text: Non-contiguous registered weights are rejected with the offending weight's name.

notes.title: Native initialization
notes.text: Bind the registry through the native load path; return models keyed by their names.

init_all.label: Validate weight buffers and initialize models in a compiled artifact.

llama_trace.purpose: Adapt flat graph inputs back into the Llama forward contract.

notes.title: Recover KV structure
notes.text: The graph boundary is flat; this adapter reconstructs the per-device KV collection required by the model.

notes.title: Trace through the constructor
notes.text: Passing forward to Graph causes the constructor to invoke it on symbolic graph inputs and finalize its returned outputs.

llama_trace.label: Adapt flat graph inputs back into the Llama forward contract.

map_pipeline.purpose: Fuse eligible structured computations and outline kernel bodies.

notes.title: Structural fusion
notes.text: Fusion is a transformation of eligible graph structure. The schedule alone does not prove which Llama operations fuse.

notes.title: Output storage
notes.text: Provide accumulating buffers after fusion, including mixed-precision handling.

notes.title: Outline bodies
notes.text: Create structured kernel bodies after view handling, then simplify their captures and invariant views.

map_pipeline.label: Fuse eligible structured computations and outline kernel bodies.

mgp_pipeline.purpose: Plan runtime resources, lower primitives, and emit Mojo routines.

notes.title: Memory planning
notes.text: Buffer reuse, allocation planning, deferral, and argument validation operate on the runtime-model representation.

notes.title: Device-graph path
notes.text: Staging, dependency computation, build stubs, and finalization are separate from the frontend Graph.output operation.

notes.title: Deduplicate routines
notes.text: Earlier canonicalization makes equivalent routines eligible for merging. Layer count is not necessarily the count of distinct generated routines.

notes.title: Emit source for JIT
notes.text: Mojo emission is at the end of this builder. The enclosing pipeline schedules kernel JIT afterward.

mgp_pipeline.label: Plan runtime resources, lower primitives, and emit Mojo routines.

mo_pipeline.purpose: Prepare and optimize high-level graph operations before MAP lowering.

notes.title: Kernel definitions
notes.text: Import/verify packages only when declarations were not already seeded by the caller.

notes.title: Shape and symbolic work
notes.text: Shape inference and constant folding are configured independently; symbolic optimization and cleanup run in this stage.

notes.title: Layouts and optional patterns
notes.text: Infer layouts and optionally run named pattern fusion before validating device information.

notes.title: Target legality
notes.text: Check device information before the final cleanup and unused-operation removal.

mo_pipeline.label: Prepare and optimize high-level graph operations before MAP lowering.

mogg_pipeline.purpose: Legalize kernel calls and outline routines.

notes.title: Call preparation
notes.text: Legalize rowwise kernels, conform operands, outline routines, and add tracing wrappers before module cleanup.

mogg_pipeline.label: Legalize kernel calls and outline routines.

native_init.purpose: Create executable model instances once compilation resolves.

notes.title: Initialize on a runtime worker
notes.text: The continuation uses the compiled artifact and captured weight registry on the CPU runtime worker.

notes.title: Executable state
notes.text: Create the executable models with runtime configuration and actual weight buffers, then resolve the result.

native_init.label: Create executable model instances once compilation resolves.

native_session.purpose: Turn the Python module capsule into a native CompilationRequest.

notes.title: Opaque source and format
notes.text: The frontend must interpret the pointer using the matching MLIR implementation and file format.
